choice.ex: (A) inherently (B) neutral (C) channel 근거 ❶❷❸❹ 해설: (A) ❶❷ inseparable → 본질적으로 연결 / (B) ❸ passive backdrop → 중립적인(아무 역할 없는) 배경 / (C) ❹ the medium of all experiences → 통로. loosely는 ❶과 반대, active는 '단지 ~한 배경으로 취급하지 말라'는 비판 대상과 맞지 않음, obstacle은 ❹와 반대. 요약문 해석: 모든 경험은 어딘가에서 일어나기 때문에, 공간은 그 안에서 일어나는 사건들과 (A) 본질적으로 연결되어 있다. 이는 장소가 단지 (B) 중립적 인 배경으로 취급되어서는 안 되며, 오히려 그것이 우리가 행동하고, 생각하고, 기억하고, 느끼는 바로 그 (C) 통로일 수 있다는 것을 의미한다.

choice.body: Every model has to treat some facts as (A)________ instead of explaining them. read.ko: 그 세계의 모든 인류는 이러한 풍요로움에 참여할 수 있도록 충분히 교육을 받아 왔다.
read.en: All of humanity in that world has been fully educated so that they can participate in this prosperity.

read.ko: 모든 사람은 탐험가, 연구원, 기술자, 예술가, 의사 또는 상담사이다.
read.en: Everyone is an explorer, researcher, engineer, artist, doctor, or counselor.

read.ko: 생성형 AI는 우리 사회의 많은 측면이 마찬가지로 매우 풍요로워질 수 있게 할 잠재력을 지니고 있다.
read.en: Generative AI has the potential to allow many dimensions of our own society to be similarly highly abundant.

read.ko: 사람들은, 고객이든 그렇지 않든, 경청받고 있다고 느끼기를 원한다.
read.en: People, whether customers or otherwise, want to feel heard.

read.ko: 누군가가 고객 서비스 센터에 전화를 하거나, 관리자와 이야기하기를 요청하거나, 마음에 어떤 생각을 품은 채 여러분의 사무실로 찾아올 때, 그들은 누군 가가 자신의 우려 사항에 귀를 기울이고 그것을 해결해 줄 것처럼 느끼기를 원한다.
read.en: When someone calls customer service, asks to speak to a manager, or comes into your office with something on their mind, they want to feel like someone is listening to their concerns and going to address them.

read.ko: 그러나 누군가가 경청받고 있다고 느끼기 위해서는, 세 가지가 이루어져야 한다.
read.en: But for someone to feel heard, three things have to happen.

read.ko: 첫째, 그들은 상대방이 자신들이 말한 것에 주의를 기울인 것처럼 느껴야 한다.
read.en: First, they have to feel like the other person paid attention to what they said.

read.ko: 둘째, 그들은 상대방이 자신들이 말한 것을 이해한 것처럼 느껴야 한다.
read.en: Second, they have to feel like the other person understood what they said.

read.ko: 그리고 셋째, 상대방은 자신이 귀를 기울였다는 것을 보여 줘야 한다.
read.en: And third, the other person has to demonstrate that they listened.

read.ko: 이 마지막 부분이 핵심이다.
read.en: This last part is key.

read.ko: 아무런 반응도 보여 주지 않는 사람과 이야기한다고 상상해 보라.
read.en: Imagine talking to someone who provided no response.

read.ko: 그들은 우리가 말한 모든 것에 주의를 기울였을지도 모른다.
read.en: They might have attended to everything we said.

read.ko: 그들은 심지어 그것을 완전히 이해했을지도 모른다.
read.en: They might even have understood it completely.

read.ko: 그러나 그들이 귀를 기울였음을 보여 주는 어떤 종류의 외적인 신호가 없이는, 그들이 실제로 그렇게 했는지 아닌지를 아는 것은 불가능하다.
read.en: But without some sort of outward signal that indicates they listened, it’s impossible to know whether or not they actually did.

read.ko: 우리의 모든 경험이 물리적 공간에서 ‘일어난다’는 바로 그 사실은, 그 공간을 그것을 규정하는 것, 즉 그 공간 ‘안’에서 일어난 사건으로부터 분리될 수 없게 만든다.
read.en: The very fact that all of our experiences “take place” in a physical space makes the space inseparable from what defines it, from the event that took place in it.

read.ko: 그 나무와 그 아래의 땅은 그곳에서 일어난 일과 분리될 수 없다.
read.en: The tree and the ground beneath are inseparable from what took place there.

read.ko: 공간, 장소, 그리고 경험의 이러한 뒤얽힘은 수동적 배경으로서의 장소라는 개념에 이의를 제기한다.
read.en: This intertwining of space, place, and experience challenges the idea of place as passive backdrop.

read.ko: 만약 장소와 공간이 경험의 바로 그 핵심의 중심이라면, 우리는 공간적 틀이 모든 경험, 즉 모든 장소에서의 행동, 생각, 기억, 그리고 감정의 매개체이며, (일반적으로 생각되는 것처럼) 단지 경험의 외부에 있는 배경이나 상황이 아니라는 가능성을 받아들여야 한다.
read.en: If place and space are central to the very heart of experience, we must accept the possibility that the spatial framework is the medium of all experiences — actions, thoughts, memories, and feelings of every place — not merely a background or context exterior to experience (as commonly supposed).

read.ko: 벨기에의 문학 평론가 Georges Poulet는 Marcel Proust의 위대한 소설 『In Search of Lost Time』에서 창조된 공간에 대해 다음과 같이 쓰면서 그 점을 유려하게 말했다. “존재들은 자신들을 발견하게 되는 장소들로 스스로를 둘러싸는데, 이는 어떤 사람이 변장인 동시에 그 사람을 특징짓는 것이기도 한 의 복으로 자신을 감싸는 것과 같다.
read.en: Belgian literary critic Georges Poulet made the point elegantly, writing of the space created in Marcel Proust’s great novel In Search of Lost Time: “Beings surround themselves with the places where they find themselves, the way one wraps oneself up in a garment that is at one and the same time a disguise and a characterization.

read.ko: 장소가 없다면, 존재들은 단지 추상적 개념에 불과할 것이다.”
read.en: Without places, beings would be only abstractions.”

read.ko: 여러분이 관심을 두는 진화 시스템(예를 들어 휴대 전화)의 경계를 어떻게 정할지 선택하든 간에, 새로운 아이디어가 특정한 시기에 출현한다는 사실 같은, 여러분의 모델이 그저 주어진 것으로 받아들여야만 하는 어떤 것들이 있을 것이다.
read.en: No matter how you choose to delineate your evolutionary system of interest — let’s say it’s cell phones — there will be some things that your model just needs to take as a given, such as the fact that new ideas emerge at particular times.

read.ko: 실제로, ‘모든’ 모델은 이러한 성격의 단순화하는 가정들을 세워야만 한다.
read.en: Indeed, all models must make simplifying assumptions of this nature.

read.ko: Wallace와 Darwin이 생물학적 진화에 대한 자신들의 언어적 모델을 제시했을 때, 변이 생성과 유전이 어떻게 작동하는지에 관해서는 거의 알지 못했다.
read.en: When Wallace and Darwin presented their verbal model of biological evolution, there was little knowledge of how variation generation and inheritance worked.

read.ko: 그들은 이러한 것들이 어떻게든 일어났다는 것을 그저 주어진 것으로 받아들였다.
read.en: They just took as a given that these things happened somehow.

read.ko: 가장 미세한 세부 수준에서조차, 우리는 단순화하는 가정들이 필요하다.
read.en: Even at the finest level of detail, we need simplifying assumptions.

read.ko: 예를 들어, 물리학자들은 기본 입자의 질량과 전하를 주어진 것으로 받아들여야만 한다.
read.en: Physicists, for example, must take as a given the mass and charge of fundamental particles.

read.ko: 원자 결합 모델에서, 물리학자들은 ‘왜’ 전자가 그것의 특정한 질량과 전하를 갖는지 설명하려 시도하지 않고, 그저 측정된 값들을 받아들이고 넘어간다.
read.en: In a model of atomic bonds, physicists don’t attempt to explain why electrons have their particular mass and charge, they just accept the measured values and move on.

read.ko: 핵심은 우리가 모든 다른 수준에서 일어나고 있는 것에 대한 완전한 설명 없이 하나의 분석 수준에서 유용한 모델을 구축할 수 있다는 것이다.
read.en: The key point is that we can build useful models at one level of analysis without a complete accounting of what’s happening at all other levels.

read.ko: 2019년 WHO에 의한 번아웃의 직업적 현상으로서의 인정은 직장에서의 정신 건강에 관한 담론에서 중요한 순간을 나타냈다.
read.en: The recognition of burnout as an occupational phenomenon by the WHO in 2019 marked an important moment in the discourse on workplace mental health.

read.ko: 이러한 지정은 임상적 평가와 조직의 책임을 재구성하여, 관심을 시스템 차원의 예방으로 이동시킨다.
read.en: This designation reframes clinical assessment and organizational responsibility, shifting attention to systemic prevention.

read.ko: 그것은 고용주들이 오직 개인 수준의 해결책에만 의존하기보다는 구조적 개입을 채택하도록 이끈다.
read.en: It invites employers to adopt structural interventions rather than relying solely on individual-level remedies.

read.ko: 실제로, 이것은 임상의들이 근본 원인을 다루기 위해 산업 보건 부서 및 지도부와 협력해야 한다는 것을 의미한다.
read.en: In practice, this means clinicians should collaborate with occupational health and leadership to address root causes.

read.ko: 그것은 번아웃을 개인적 실패나 개인의 회복 탄력성의 문제로 보는 것에서 벗어나, 그것을 조직 문화, 지도부 관행, 그리고 더 넓은 노동의 사회 경제적 맥 락에 뿌리를 둔 구조적 문제로 이해하는 것으로 향하는 전환을 나타냈다.
read.en: It signaled a shift away from viewing burnout as a personal failing or a matter of individual resilience, toward understanding it as a structural issue rooted in organizational culture, leadership practices, and the broader socio-economic context of work.

read.ko: 이 재구성은 필수적인데, 왜냐하면 그것은 오직 개인에게만 대처하거나 적응하도록 부담을 지우기보다는 시스템 차원의 개입과 정책 수준의 변화로 향하 는 문을 열어 주기 때문이다.
read.en: This reframing is essential, as it opens the door to systemic interventions and policy-level changes rather than placing the burden solely on individuals to cope or adapt.

para.en: Subsidies, taxes, and regulations can all lead to power plants that pollute less by switching away from coal. In all cases, profits can be higher from making the transition, even taking the related costs into account. The power plants prefer subsidies over regulations or taxes. The reason is obvious. They prefer to receive money from the government rather than pay the costs themselves. But the “expansion” of their opportunity set through subsidies has to be matched by the contraction of the opportunity set of others. The electricity companies’ “freedom” is increased at the expense of the ordinary individual, who must suffer from increased taxation to pay for the subsidy. Moreover, from the perspective of pure efficiency, the subsidy distorts the economy because the electricity company is not facing the full costs of what it does, even if it is successful in limiting emissions. Indeed, electricity prices may end up lower than they should be and electricity consumption higher, which will worsen global warming, even though the emissions per unit of electricity have been reduced.

Few people may view the Star Trek universe through an economic lens, but doing so provides a window into a world that might soon be upon us. All of classical economics is based on the notion that there isn’t usually enough of anything to give everyone everything they want or need. Because of that, we use markets and pricing to allocate those goods, services, and resources to where they might result in the highest benefit. In Star Trek, however, there isn’t much scarcity. Technology has allowed that society to reproduce any food they want, transport themselves thousands of miles in the blink of an eye, communicate over light-years, and travel among the stars. All of humanity in that world has been fully educated so that they can participate in this prosperity. Everyone is an explorer, researcher, engineer, artist, doctor, or counselor. Generative AI has the potential to allow many dimensions of our own society to be similarly highly abundant.

People, whether customers or otherwise, want to feel heard. When someone calls customer service, asks to speak to a manager, or comes into your office with something on their mind, they want to feel like someone is listening to their concerns and going to address them. But for someone to feel heard, three things have to happen. First, they have to feel like the other person paid attention to what they said. Second, they have to feel like the other person understood what they said. And third, the other person has to demonstrate that they listened. This last part is key. Imagine talking to someone who provided no response. They might have attended to everything we said. They might even have understood it completely. But without some sort of outward signal that indicates they listened, it’s impossible to know whether or not they actually did.

The very fact that all of our experiences “take place” in a physical space makes the space inseparable from what defines it, from the event that took place in it. The tree and the ground beneath are inseparable from what took place there. This intertwining of space, place, and experience challenges the idea of place as passive backdrop. If place and space are central to the very heart of experience, we must accept the possibility that the spatial framework is the medium of all experiences — actions, thoughts, memories, and feelings of every place — not merely a background or context exterior to experience (as commonly supposed). Belgian literary critic Georges Poulet made the point elegantly, writing of the space created in Marcel Proust’s great novel In Search of Lost Time: “Beings surround themselves with the places where they find themselves, the way one wraps oneself up in a garment that is at one and the same time a disguise and a characterization. Without places, beings would be only abstractions.”

No matter how you choose to delineate your evolutionary system of interest — let’s say it’s cell phones — there will be some things that your model just needs to take as a given, such as the fact that new ideas emerge at particular times. Indeed, all models must make simplifying assumptions of this nature. When Wallace and Darwin presented their verbal model of biological evolution, there was little knowledge of how variation generation and inheritance worked. They just took as a given that these things happened somehow. Even at the finest level of detail, we need simplifying assumptions. Physicists, for example, must take as a given the mass and charge of fundamental particles. In a model of atomic bonds, physicists don’t attempt to explain why electrons have their particular mass and charge, they just accept the measured values and move on. The key point is that we can build useful models at one level of analysis without a complete accounting of what’s happening at all other levels.

The recognition of burnout as an occupational phenomenon by the WHO in 2019 marked an important moment in the discourse on workplace mental health. This designation reframes clinical assessment and organizational responsibility, shifting attention to systemic prevention. It invites employers to adopt structural interventions rather than relying solely on individual-level remedies. In practice, this means clinicians should collaborate with occupational health and leadership to address root causes. It signaled a shift away from viewing burnout as a personal failing or a matter of individual resilience, toward understanding it as a structural issue rooted in organizational culture, leadership practices, and the broader socio-economic context of work. This reframing is essential, as it opens the door to systemic interventions and policy-level changes rather than placing the burden solely on individuals to cope or adapt.

howto.cloze: 빈칸을 하나씩 보여 줘요. 우리말 뜻·유의어·첫 글자 힌트를 보고 원문 표현 그대로 쓰고 Enter(또는 다음 빈칸)를 누르세요. 빈칸을 모두 채워야 다음 지문으로 넘어가요.
howto.tf: 글과 일치하면 T, 아니면 F를 누르세요. 문장을 하나씩 보여 주고, 누르면 다음 문장으로 넘어가요. 지문은 아래 상자 안에서 스크롤하며 읽어요. 결과 화면에서 F 문장의 고칠 부분과 근거를 확인하세요.
howto.choice: 요약문 빈칸 · 추론할 수 없는 것 · 밑줄 의미를 고르는 5지선다예요. 지문은 상자 안에서 스크롤해요.
howto.order: 단락 (A)~(D)를 원래 글의 순서대로 눌러 주세요. 원문은 볼 수 없어요.
howto.insert: 주어진 문장이 들어갈 번호를 누르세요. 원문은 볼 수 없어요.
